title: Redesign the Operator's Board
question: The roll dealt three compositions for /board inside the committed world. Lock one — or steer and re-roll.

options.label: The Ledger Spread
options.lineage: switchboard position log / operator's daily logbook
options.thesis: Every line is one ledger row — jack, state, usage, action — scanned top to bottom like a position log.
options.viewport: Header plus a summary strip (live / on hold / credits), then one ledger row per line with inline plug and unplug, the plug-in CTA closing the page.
options.risk: Reads like a spreadsheet the moment the jack character or the amber ration slips.

regions.label: summary strip · live / on hold / credits

options.label: The Instrument Cluster
options.thesis: The glance lives up top: gauges for lines live, conversations used, and credits left, with the board beneath.
options.viewport: Three dial-face gauges across the top viewport with the jack rows below; nothing else competes for the first look.
options.risk: Gauges eat the first viewport and push the board below the fold on laptops.

options.label: The Split Desk
options.lineage: switchboard position with its instrument shelf
options.thesis: Board on the left, a permanent instrument shelf on the right — usage, activity, shortcuts — nothing behind navigation.
options.viewport: Two panes: jack rows left, the shelf right with the usage meter, recent activity, and quick actions always visible.
options.risk: The shelf collapses on narrow screens and the glance becomes a scroll.
